Container.Name: eugene-plexus
Container.Overview:
A self-hosted control plane for local LLM inference. It supervises engine processes it does not own, keeps a model library on your own disk as plainly-named files, holds per-model settings, and exposes one OpenAI-compatible endpoint that load-balances and fails over across local runtimes and cloud subscriptions — with real auth, so it works over a tailnet and not just localhost.
THIS CONTAINER IS THE CONTROL PLANE ONLY. There is no GPU in here and no inference engine, by design. Point your tools at port 8080; run the installer on each machine that has a GPU and join it to port 8083. One click here does not give you a model — it gives you the thing that manages them.
PRE-RELEASE. The image is tagged `edge`, there is no released version, and the API may change. It is used daily by its author across two machines; it has not been used by anybody else.
FIRST START: open the WebUI and finish the wizard. It sets the passphrase that owns this install, so do it promptly — until then the first person to reach port 8079 can claim it.
RESTARTS: the trust root comes back sealed and routes nothing until somebody unlocks it, because a container has no OS keyring. Either unlock it on the Nodes page after each restart, or set up the passphrase file below once and stop thinking about it.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: The web interface, and the browser's pass-through to every component. This is the port you open.

Config.Name: OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Config.Description: Point your tools and agent harnesses here. Speaks /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models, with tool calling and token streaming.

Config.Name: Control root
Config.Description: Where machines with GPUs enroll, and where a warm standby follows the log. If you change this, every node you have already enrolled is pointing at the old one — they record the address, not the name.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: THIS DIRECTORY IS THE INSTALL. It holds the identity and enrollment (agent.yaml, node.yaml), the trust root's replicated log, retained request metrics, and the logs. Keep it across updates and an update is an update; point at a fresh one and you have built a second install whose worker nodes are still enrolled to a root that no longer exists. Back it up. IT MUST BE OWNED BY 99:100 (nobody:users), which is what this container runs as: run `chown -R 99:100` on it before you start, and especially if it was created by an older container that ran as a different user.

Config.Name: Passphrase file (optional)
Config.Description: Set this AND the variable below to make restarts unattended. Put your passphrase in a file (use printf, not echo — one trailing newline is tolerated but nothing else is trimmed), chmod 400 it, and point this at it. Then set Security mode to 'Passphrase file auto-unlock' once in the web UI. Leave both blank and the trust root comes back sealed after every restart until you unlock it by hand. What it trades away: anyone who can read that file can unlock this install without knowing the passphrase.

Config.Name: Passphrase file path (optional)
Config.Description: The container-side path of the file above — /run/secrets/passphrase if you used the default. Set both or neither: set this alone and the root logs that the file is missing and stays sealed.

Config.Name: Safe mode
Config.Description: Set to 1 to recover an install whose agent.yaml will not parse. The config endpoints stay reachable so the web UI can fix it. Leave at 0.
